about: Verification of every second-review finding that the first review did not have (2026-11-16): Claude Opus 5.5 with web access checked each against the summary, the method and outside sources, and kept, corrected or dropped it. Three weak sources were replaced afterwards (Sabra and Shatila, Twelve-Day War, Black Friday).

fairness.note: Says the king and crown prince "were executed" and does not mention that they were shot in the palace courtyard, without trial, together with women of the royal family and servants (Arab News, 2018).
phrases: were executed

sources.claim: On 14 July 1958 King Faisal II and other members of his family were rounded up in the palace courtyard and shot; those killed included Crown Prince Abd al-Ilah, Princess Nafisa and Princess Abadiya.

fairness.reason: Omission of the other royal victims is real; reworded to state the facts instead of the inference about 'legal process'.

wording.note: Calls the event a military coup in Wikipedia's own voice and elsewhere speaks of "revolutionary forces". It gives both names but does not say that the choice between them is disputed.
wording.reason: Revolution-or-coup is a listed contested characterisation; same standard as the 1952 Egyptian entry.

fairness.reason: The text states acts (conquest and depopulation, which historians across schools accept happened), not that depopulation was the plan's aim, and "in preparation for the establishment of a Jewish state" matches the plan's stated purpose. "Invasion" is the standard term, and the sentence gives the Arab states' aim of taking the Arab areas. The note says nothing specific about the last sentence.

wording.phrase: Although the causes of the 1948 Palestinian exodus remain a significantly controversial topic
wording.reason: "Although" contrasts public debate with a scholarly view that is attributed ("most scholarship today agrees"); it does not invent a relationship. The steering word in the sentence, "denialism", is already flagged in the published review.

wording.note: Calls the referendum "controversial" in Wikipedia's own voice without saying who disputed it or why.
wording.reason: "Controversial" is on the MOS:LABEL list, which asks to describe the controversy instead.

fairness.note: Says the coup was carried out against "the democratically elected government" and led to executions, but gives no reason the officers acted. Their stated aims, ending the political crisis and returning to Atatürk's reforms, and their charge that the Democrat Party government was repressing the opposition, are not mentioned (GlobalSecurity; academic accounts of the coup).
phrases: democratically elected government of the Democrat Party

sources.claim: The National Unity Committee's stated purpose was to return Turkey to Atatürk's reforms and prevent a return to political chaos.
Academic work attributes the coup's reasons in part to the authoritarian attitude of Menderes towards the opposition.

fairness.reason: The absence is real and the officers' stated reasons are central to a coup. 'Authoritarian' softened to the officers' charge of repressing the opposition, attributed.

fairness.note: States as fact, without saying whose figure it is, that the purges replaced "90% of its officer corps with Alawites". Published scholarship describes a large rise in Alawite and other minority officers after the purges, in which about 700 officers were dismissed, but the accounts found do not give this figure (Sorby, Asian and African Studies).
phrases: replacing 90% of its officer corps with Alawites

sources.claim: About 700 officers were dismissed after the coup and minority officers increased at the expense of Sunnis; no 90% figure is given.

fairness.reason: Kept only the unattributed 90% figure. The judgement words about Ba'athist rule ('totalitarian', 'brutal repression') describe well-documented repression, and 'state terror' is already in the published wording point; 'unfolding conspiracy' is plain narrative. Treated the same as 'brutal' in the 1991 Iraqi uprisings entry.

fairness.note: Says in Wikipedia's own voice that the insurrection was "brutally suppressed", a judgement word with no attribution. Neither the government's nor the Muslim Brotherhood's stated position is given.
phrases: brutally suppressed
fairness.reason: Accurate: "brutally" is unattributed and the text gives no position from either side. No outside claims.
Unattributed superlatives, but they do not tell the story from one side or favour a party; too marginal for a fairness finding, and not listed puffery words.

wording.reason: The text's own Arabic name is "inqilāb" (coup); "Revolution" is the name, and the coup description of a military seizure by the Ba'ath is not meaningfully contested.

fairness.note: Gives Israel's reason for the raid in Wikipedia's own voice and says nothing of the response to it. The UN Security Council unanimously condemned the raid in Resolution 262 (31 December 1968), which is not mentioned.
phrases: in retaliation for the attack

sources.claim: UN Security Council Resolution 262 (1968), adopted unanimously, condemned Israel for the premeditated military action at Beirut airport

fairness.reason: The UNSC condemnation is confirmed and absent from the text. Lebanon's denial of responsibility could not be verified, so it was removed.

wording.note: "A convenient pretext" sits outside the quotation marks and imputes a motive to Iran's leadership in Wikipedia's own voice, adding an argument.
wording.reason: The words are unquoted; imputing motive is an argument in Wikipedia's voice. Both review types may point to the same words.

fairness.note: Gives only the official result. It does not mention that several groups, including followers of Ayatollah Shariatmadari and most secular parties, called for a boycott, or that turnout was low in Kurdistan and Azerbaijan (Iran Chamber Society; Boroumand Center).
phrases: approved by 99.5% of voters

sources.claim: Most secular parties called for a boycott; Shariatmadari opposed the constitution and boycotted; turnout was low in Kurdish areas and Azerbaijan.
Shariatmadari opposed the constitution's clerical provisions.

fairness.reason: Boycott and low regional turnout confirmed. Removed the comparison with another event's summary, which was not checked.

'Brutal' describes a suppression the text itself documents (summary executions, indiscriminate attacks on civilians), which is well established; 'regime' is not a listed word. Same standard as the Syrian entry's judgement words.

fairness.note: States the American and British reason as the cause of the strikes in Wikipedia's own voice. It reports criticism of the bombing but not Iraq's position, including its charge that the inspectors spied for the United States, which was later partly borne out by reports that U.S. intelligence used inspection equipment to eavesdrop (Washington Post, 1999).
phrases: The strikes were launched due to Iraq's failure to comply

sources.claim: U.S. intelligence secretly used UNSCOM equipment to eavesdrop on Iraqi communications.
Iraq accused the inspectors of spying for the United States.

fairness.reason: Holds; added the reported basis for Iraq's charge, attributed.

fairness.note: Says the men were hanged during the Armenian genocide but not by whom or why. They were sentenced by an Ottoman court-martial on charges of "high treason and separatism" (ANI Armenian Research Center).
phrases: Hunchakian activists who were hanged

sources.claim: The accused were tried by an Ottoman court-martial in Constantinople under General Nafiz Bey, and twenty were condemned to death for "high treason and separatism"; they were hanged on 15 June 1915.

fairness.reason: Absence of perpetrator and charge confirmed in the text; charges found in a specialist source. Reworded to give the actual charge.

fairness.note: Describes the AKP's politics as "moderate Islamism" in Wikipedia's own voice and leaves out the party's own description of itself as "conservative democrat", rejecting the Islamist label (Congressional Research Service, 2002).
phrases: The moderate Islamism advocated by the AKP

sources.claim: The AKP eschews the label 'Islamist', preferring 'conservative democrat'

fairness.reason: The text states it unattributed and gives no self-description; the party's rejection of the label is documented.

wording.note: Calls the by-election "controversial" in Wikipedia's own voice without saying who disputed it or why.
wording.reason: "Controversial" is on the MOS:LABEL list; unquoted and unattributed.

fairness.note: Calls the government an authoritarian regime twice in Wikipedia's own voice, without attribution, and reports the accusations of intimidation and vote buying with no response from the government or the election authorities.
phrases: the authoritarian Hosni Mubarak regime
the authoritarian regime
fairness.reason: Both statements about the text are accurate; no outside claim is made.

wording.note: Nour's figure for his own support gets "claimed", while the government's vote figures are given as what "official results" were "showing".
wording.reason: Uneven verbs for comparable vote-share statements by two parties. The opposition's "said" is the same side, so it was removed from the note.

fairness.note: Lists factors behind Ahmadinejad's victory but does not mention that first-round candidates Mehdi Karroubi and Akbar Rafsanjani alleged interference in the vote, including by the Basij and Revolutionary Guards (RFE/RL, 2005).
phrases: Factors thought to have contributed to Ahmadinejad's victory

sources.claim: Karroubi wrote to Khamenei alleging illegal intervention by the Revolutionary Guards and multiple voting by Basij members; Rafsanjani backed the complaint

fairness.reason: The omission of the fraud complaints is real. "Corrupt elite insiders" sits inside a hedged list of factors and describes voters' motive, not the losing camp in Wikipedia's voice, so that part was dropped.

fairness.note: States in Wikipedia's own voice that the Abdullah Azzam Brigades committed the bombings, and gives their aim as a strategy against tourism. Responsibility rested on that group's unverified claim; two other groups also claimed the attacks, and Egyptian authorities attributed them to Sinai Bedouin militants from the group behind the 2004 Taba bombings (Al Jazeera, 2005).
phrases: were committed by Islamist group Abdullah Azzam Brigades
was part of a strategy of damaging tourism

sources.claim: The Abdullah Azzam Brigades claimed the bombings in a statement whose authenticity could not be verified.
Egyptian authorities said the same Sinai Bedouin group carried out the Sharm el-Sheikh and Taba bombings.
Other groups (Holy Warriors of Egypt, Egyptian Tawheed wal Jihad) also claimed the attacks.

fairness.reason: Point holds; the 'other groups were also blamed' wording was vague and is replaced by the specific competing claims and the Egyptian government's attribution.

fairness.note: Gives Israel's stated objectives and the Israeli government's rocket count, attributed, but no casualty figures for either side; the UN counted 198 Palestinians killed in Gaza in June and July 2006 alone (UN OCHA, 2006).
phrases: Israel's stated objectives in Operation Summer Rains
757 missiles from Gaza hit Israel

sources.claim: UN OCHA: 198 Palestinians, including 44 children, killed in the Gaza Strip in June and July 2006

fairness.reason: The missing casualty figures are a real omission. "Prompted by the capture" is the standard account of the trigger, and the unspecified 'Palestinian account' of earlier events was unsupported; both removed.

fairness.note: Gives the operation's aim, which the IDF stated (OCHA situation report, 2006), as a fact in Wikipedia's own voice. The only Palestinian voice is officials announcing the withdrawal; no Palestinian view of the operation is given.
phrases: The operation was launched to stop Palestinian rocket attacks into Israel

sources.claim: The IDF's stated purpose for the operation was to stop home-made rockets being fired into Israel.

fairness.reason: Stated aim as fact and absent Palestinian view hold. The unsourced civilian figure is dropped: an unattributed casualty count is not one-sided in itself.

fairness.note: Says Israel attacked Lebanese civilian infrastructure, while Hezbollah's rocket fire is described without saying that it struck Israeli towns and killed civilians (Human Rights Watch, 2007). It places the opening raid "on the border" without saying that Hezbollah fighters crossed into Israel (UN Secretary-General, 12 July 2006). The death figures are given without saying how many were civilians on either side.
phrases: Lebanese civilian infrastructure
launched more rockets into northern Israel
ambushed Israeli soldiers on the border

sources.claim: Hezbollah rockets fired at times deliberately at civilian areas in northern Israel killed at least 39 civilians
The UN Secretary-General condemned Hezbollah's attack across the Blue Line on 12 July 2006

fairness.reason: All three points check out against the text and sources; added citations.

wording.note: The IDF's statement about the strike gets "admitted", while the residents' statement about the same strike in the next sentence gets "said".
wording.reason: "Admit" is on the MOS:SAID list and the comparable statements by two parties get different verbs.

fairness.note: Calls Abdullah Gül "an Islamist politician" in Wikipedia's own voice. His party rejected the Islamist label and Gül pledged during the campaign to uphold secular principles (CRS, 2002; Jerusalem Post, 2007); neither is given.
phrases: an Islamist politician

sources.claim: The AKP eschews the label 'Islamist', preferring 'conservative democrat'
Gül vowed to uphold secular principles as presidential candidate in 2007

fairness.reason: No source found where Gül himself rejected the label (reports speak of his 'Islamist past'), so the note now says what is documented: the party's rejection and his secular pledge.

wording.phrase: he claimed 14 million unused ballots were missing
wording.note: Mousavi's statement about missing ballots gets "claimed", while the Guardian Council's statement about the same election in the sentence before is given as what it "concluded".
wording.reason: Comparable statements about the vote's integrity by two parties get uneven verbs; "claim" is on the MOS:SAID list.

fairness.note: Gives the reason for the crackdown, "the sporadic cases of violence present at the protests", in Wikipedia's own voice rather than attributing it to the government.
phrases: Due to the sporadic cases of violence present at the protests
fairness.reason: The unattributed justification is real. The beatings and abuse in detention are widely documented and the authorities themselves acknowledged abuses at Kahrizak, so 'without the government's response' does not hold; that part was dropped.

wording.note: "Despite" sets the announced result against the reported irregularities in Wikipedia's own voice, inviting the reader to doubt the result.
wording.reason: Listed word, Wikipedia's voice, steers toward the opposition's reading.

fairness.note: States the government's aim for the changes in Wikipedia's own voice. It leaves out the position of the opposition CHP, which argued that changing the make-up of the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Board of Judges and Prosecutors would bring the judiciary under the governing AKP's control (Hürriyet Daily News, 2010).
phrases: The changes were aimed at bringing the constitution into compliance with European Union standards

sources.claim: The CHP argued the AKP aimed to bring the judiciary under its control by changing the Constitutional Court and HSYK set-up.
The AKP said the amendments were meant to promote democracy and support Turkey's EU bid; the CHP challenged them in the Constitutional Court.

fairness.reason: The point holds. Replaced "general knowledge" with a cited source and named the party.

fairness.note: Describes the IAEA report as "highlighting evidence of weaponization" in Wikipedia's own voice and does not give Iran's response that the report was politically motivated and rested on fabricated information (Iranian officials, November 2011). The reaction is summed up in Wikipedia's voice as shock to "the international community".
phrases: highlighting evidence of weaponization in Iran's nuclear program
shocked the international community

sources.claim: Iran rejected the November 2011 IAEA report as politically motivated and based on fabricated charges

fairness.reason: Text checks out; 'Iran's stated position that its programme is peaceful' replaced by Iran's actual response to the report, which is the directly relevant omission.

wording.note: "However" sets the Israeli strikes against the PRC's denial in the sentence before, a relationship stated in Wikipedia's own voice rather than by a source.
wording.reason: "However" is on the MOS:EDITORIAL list of contrast words; in Wikipedia's voice it implies the strikes went ahead in spite of the denial, which steers the reader.

fairness.note: Gives two judgements in Wikipedia's own voice rather than as what protesters said: the SCAF's "apparent power grab" (hedged only by "apparent") and that the film was discriminating against Islam.
phrases: the apparent power grab by the SCAF
the film discriminating Islam
fairness.reason: Point holds, but the note said the text states a power grab outright; it is hedged with 'apparent'.

fairness.note: States in Wikipedia's own voice that these were the only democratic presidential elections in Egypt's history; the last paragraph gives a similar point as what is "broadly considered". It also calls some candidates moderate or pro-democracy and the likely majority choice without saying who judges so.
phrases: these are the only democratic presidential elections in Egyptian history
moderate or pro-democracy candidates
the likely majority-preferred candidates
fairness.reason: All three statements are unattributed in the text; the note describes only the text.

fairness.note: Both sides' stated reasons and claims of victory are given. The effects in Israel are told in more detail (named cities, a breakdown of where rockets fell, people treated for anxiety) than in Gaza, where the 174 dead are not divided into civilians and combatants; B'Tselem counted 87 civilians among 167 Palestinians killed (B'Tselem, 2013).
phrases: 174 Palestinians were killed
treated for anxiety

sources.claim: B'Tselem found 167 Palestinians were killed, 87 of them civilians not taking part in hostilities.

fairness.reason: Imbalance of detail holds. 'Civilians counted separately' for Israel was overstated: the six Israeli dead are not divided either, only the three killed in Kiryat Malachi are called civilians.

fairness.note: States in Wikipedia's own voice that the bombardment was a response to a Free Syrian Army attack, the explanation given by sources on the government side. The charge that the shelling was indiscriminate appears only through the government's denial, and no civilian death figures are given, though activists reported more than 200 killed in the shelling of 4 February (Al Jazeera, 2012).
phrases: in response to an attack by the Free Syrian Army

sources.claim: Activists said more than 200 people were killed in the shelling of Homs on 4 February 2012.

fairness.reason: Point holds; added whose explanation the 'response' framing is and the scale of the omitted civilian toll, with a source.

fairness.note: Describes the clearing of the sit-ins as a "massacre" and the protests as "violently suppressed" in Wikipedia's own voice. The government's death figure is given, but not its stated position that force was used in response to violence, including gunfire, by protesters (Human Rights Watch report, 2014).
phrases: violently suppressed
dispersal and massacre of pro-Morsi sit-ins

sources.claim: Egyptian officials said the use of force came in response to violence, including gunfire, by protesters.

fairness.reason: Point holds for the dispersal. The claim that the government's position on Morsi's removal is missing was dropped: the text gives the ultimatum and the mass protests that preceded it.

fairness.note: Gives the 98.1% approval with no context. It leaves out that the vote was part of the roadmap after the military's removal of President Morsi, that many parties and movements boycotted it, and that observers found little room for opponents to campaign, including arrests of people posting "no" materials (Democracy International observation mission, 2014).
phrases: approved by 98.1% of voters

sources.claim: Democracy International said the referendum took place against arrests of dissenting voices, there was no real opportunity to dissent, Strong Egypt members were arrested for posting "no" materials, and many parties boycotted.
The Muslim Brotherhood-led alliance boycotted the referendum and arrests were reported during the vote.

fairness.reason: Confirmed by an observer mission. Replaced "general knowledge" with sources.

fairness.note: States in Wikipedia's own voice that the election was neither free nor fair and was marred by irregularities, repression and suppression of free speech. None of this is attributed, although observers differed: the EU mission said the vote was administered in line with the law while noting a restricted environment, and Democracy International said repression prevented a genuine democratic election (preliminary statements, May 2014).
phrases: which was neither free nor fair
marred by irregularities, repression of el-Sisi's political opponents, and suppression of free speech

sources.claim: EU EOM preliminary statement: election administered in line with the law, in an environment falling short of constitutional principles
Democracy International said disregard for rights and freedoms prevented a genuine democratic election; comparison of the two observer statements

fairness.reason: Text claims verified; 'Egyptian authorities' position' was unsourced, replaced by the documented split among observers.

fairness.note: States in Wikipedia's own voice that the vast majority of those killed were Gazan civilians. Further down, the summary itself shows the civilian share is disputed, from 70 percent by the Gaza Health Ministry to 36 percent by Israeli officials.
phrases: the vast majority of which were Gazan Palestinian civilians
fairness.reason: Both statements are checked against the text itself: the opening claim is unattributed, and the later estimates include 36% by Israeli officials.

wording.phrase: despite no official intifada being organized
wording.note: "Despite" adds a comment in Wikipedia's own voice on whether the news sources' term "intifada" is apt.
wording.reason: Listed word, unattributed, and it adds an argument against the term in Wikipedia's voice.

fairness.note: Gives the operation's purpose as the search for the teenagers in Wikipedia's own voice and mentions the arrest of around 350 Palestinians, but not the Palestinians killed during the operation (three by 20 June, according to the UN Special Coordinator).
phrases: in search of the three teenagers

sources.claim: By 20 June 2014 the Israeli operations had resulted in over 300 Palestinians arrested and three killed.

fairness.reason: 'Only as a search' was inaccurate (the arrests are mentioned). The point about Hamas's response was dropped: Hamas's statements changed over time and their omission does not clearly favour either side.

fairness.note: The assessments given come from scholars and from governments and officials critical of the election, with attribution. The position of the Syrian government and of the countries that accepted the result is not given; Russia's foreign ministry, for example, called the vote free and transparent (TASS, June 2014).
phrases: decried the election as illegitimate

sources.claim: Russian Foreign Ministry said the Syrian presidential election was held in a free, fair and transparent atmosphere
Russia praised the election and criticised the Western reaction

fairness.reason: Point holds; note now covers the 'scholarly consensus' sentence accurately and names a source for the accepting side's position.

wording.phrase: thus undermining and obliterating any sense of Iraqi national unity
wording.note: Adds an argument about the effect of the quota agreements in Wikipedia's own voice.
wording.reason: Unattributed argument inside a parenthesis; an argument in Wikipedia's voice is covered by EDITORIAL.

wording.phrase: pointed out that Turkey had the right to defend its airspace
wording.reason: The published SAID point already says Erdoğan "pointed out" presents his statement as true, against Russia's "claiming".
Same point as the published NPOV finding: Rubin's arguments listed in Wikipedia's own voice ("Unlike previous coups...").

wording.phrase: just 8 days after the coup attempt
wording.note: "Just" stresses how soon the closures came, in Wikipedia's own voice. This supports the suggestion that they were prepared in advance.
wording.reason: MOS:EDITORIAL names "just" (with "only") as implying something contrary to expectations. It is unattributed here and not covered by the published review.

wording.phrase: shaking the very pillars of this regime
wording.note: Adds an assessment of the protests' effect in Wikipedia's own voice, without attribution.
wording.reason: Unattributed evaluative argument in Wikipedia's voice; wording and fairness reviews may cite the same words.

fairness.note: Adds in Wikipedia's own voice that such foreign campaigning is illegal under Turkish law (the ban in Article 94/A of the election law, as reported in 2017). Turkey's stated objections to the Dutch ban are not given; its side appears only as Erdoğan's insults (Turkish foreign minister's statements, March 2017).
phrases: Such foreign campaigning is illegal under Turkish law.

sources.claim: Article 94/A of Turkey's election law bans campaigning abroad; a CHP lawmaker said no penalty attaches
Turkish foreign minister criticised the Netherlands over the rally ban

fairness.reason: Point holds; 'without a source named' dropped (leads do not cite in text) and the law's existence confirmed.

fairness.note: After Netanyahu's attribution to the Islamic State, the summary says in Wikipedia's own voice that it was "raising questions about how he came to that conclusion", without saying who raised them, and then gives opponents' criticism. It does not give what Netanyahu said, that "according to all the signs" the attacker was a supporter of the Islamic State (Ynet, 2017).
phrases: raising questions about how he came to that conclusion
Opponents criticized the Israeli government for downplaying the political side

sources.claim: Netanyahu said that according to all the signs the attacker was a supporter of ISIS

fairness.reason: Point holds; "basis the Israeli government stated" overstated, as he gave no evidence beyond "all the signs", so the note now quotes what he said.

wording.phrase: raising questions about how he came to that conclusion
wording.note: Adds a comment on Netanyahu's statement in Wikipedia's own voice, without saying who raised the questions.
wording.reason: An argument in Wikipedia's voice, unattributed.

fairness.reason: "Failed bid" describes the outcome the text itself documents. The text names the Iraqi central government as the other party in the conflict, so the agency point is marginal.

wording.note: "Despite" sets the Kurdistan Regional Government's description of the referendum as binding against an earlier report, in Wikipedia's own voice. This presents its statements as inconsistent.
wording.reason: "Despite" is a listed word, it is unattributed, and it steers toward the KRG being inconsistent. It is separate from the published SAID point on "claimed".

fairness.note: Gives the United States' reason for the strike and quotes President Trump. Leaves out the Syrian government's denial that it carried out the chemical attack (Assad, AFP interview, April 2017), and the Syrian and Russian position that the strike was an act of aggression (Kremlin statement, 7 April 2017).
phrases: as a direct response to the Khan Shaykhun chemical attack

sources.claim: Assad called the Khan Shaykhun attack a '100 percent fabrication'
Kremlin called the strike aggression against a sovereign state

fairness.reason: Both omissions verified in the text and documented in sources.

fairness.note: Reports accusations by Iranian officials that the American, Israeli and Saudi governments were behind the attacks, and quotes an IRGC commander's accusation against Saudi Arabia at length. It gives no response from the accused governments; Saudi Foreign Minister Adel al-Jubeir denied involvement (Arab News, 2017).
phrases: accused the American, Israeli, and Saudi governments of being behind the attacks
carried out at the demand of Riyadh

sources.claim: Saudi Foreign Minister Adel al-Jubeir denied Saudi involvement in the Tehran attacks

fairness.reason: Absence verified and denial sourced; note names who denied.

wording.note: Uses "terror" for the attack in Wikipedia's own voice, without saying who uses the label.
wording.reason: Listed label variant, unattributed, in a sentence the published review does not cover.

fairness.note: Calls the electoral council's acceptance of unstamped ballots "unprecedented" in Wikipedia's own voice, and reports the critics' and observers' view that it was illegal. It leaves out the council's stated position. Its chairman Sadi Güven said the decision was not unprecedented and that the ballots were valid (Hürriyet Daily News, 17 April 2017).
phrases: In an unprecedented move

sources.claim: YSK chairman Sadi Güven said the decision was not unprecedented and that the ballots and envelopes produced by the YSK were valid.

fairness.reason: "Unprecedented" in Wikipedia's voice contradicts the council's own stated position, which is absent. Dropped the phrase "declared the YSK's decision to be illegal" because it is attributed to OSCE/PACE.

fairness.note: States in Wikipedia's own voice that most demonstrators were peaceful. Israel's account appears in two short sentences against detailed casualty figures and condemnations, and the UN commission's finding that the other cases were illegal is reported without saying that Israel rejected the report (Israeli government, February 2019).
phrases: Most of the demonstrators demonstrated peacefully
The commission deemed the rest of the cases illegal

sources.claim: Israel rejected the UN commission's report, calling it 'theatre of the absurd' and biased

fairness.reason: Israel's view gets two sentences (Hamas cover; government praised troops), not one; the 223-killed phrase is a figure, not a contested framing, so removed.

fairness.note: States in Wikipedia's own voice that the election took place amid a repression campaign by el-Sisi and that this repression made all opposition candidates withdraw. The criticism by rights groups is attributed, but these sentences are not, and the Egyptian government's rejection of such criticism is not given (Egyptian Foreign Ministry, March 2018).
phrases: amid a repression campaign by incumbent President el-Sisi
In the face of this repression

sources.claim: Egypt's Foreign Ministry condemned the UN rights chief's criticism ahead of the vote as baseless

fairness.reason: Main point holds; 'pro-government politician' removed as Moussa had openly backed Sisi, which is not contested.

fairness.note: Calls the government's response "brutal" and states as fact that Iranian-backed militias helped it, both in Wikipedia's own voice. Leaves out the government's account: the military command said it had no orders to use live fire and officials blamed some deaths on unidentified snipers, though a government inquiry later found excessive force (Reuters, October 2019).
phrases: with the help of Iranian-backed militias responded brutally

sources.claim: Government inquiry found 157 killed through excessive force and said the government had not ordered live fire
Reuters reported, citing security officials, that Iran-backed militias deployed snipers; militia leaders denied it

fairness.reason: Point holds; per the paragraph rule the militia role in the same sentence is also stated as fact.

fairness.note: Gives only the proposed changes and the official result. It leaves out that Human Rights Watch said the vote was marred by reports of voters being forced or bribed with food and money, and by arrests of critics and the blocking of a campaign website (Human Rights Watch, 2019).
phrases: approved by 88.83% of voters

sources.claim: HRW said the referendum was marred by serious flaws, including reports of citizens being forced to vote or bribed, arrests of critics and the blocking of the "Batel" campaign website.
A rights group denounced the vote as unfree and unfair.

fairness.reason: The point holds. Replaced "general knowledge" with sourced, specific criticisms.

fairness.note: Ties the results blackout, in Wikipedia's own voice, to the moment the opposition was "on the verge of victory" in Istanbul. Says the Electoral Board invalidated the HDP winners' elections without giving its stated reason: that they had been dismissed from public service by emergency decree, which it said barred them from office (Supreme Election Council ruling, April 2019).
phrases: just when the opposition were on the verge of victory
invalidated the successful election

sources.claim: The YSK ruled that mayors-elect dismissed by decree law could not take office and gave the mandates to runners-up

fairness.reason: Blackout framing and missing YSK reason hold; 'initiated mainly by the AK Party' is a factual description of who filed, and the Istanbul grounds belong to the rerun's own entry.

wording.reason: The published SAID finding already notes that Turkey's claim is set against the experts' view with "Although".

fairness.note: Says the Houthis were suspected of carrying out the attack but does not say who suspected them or give the Houthis' own position; they denied responsibility (Bellingcat, 2021).
phrases: suspected of carrying out the attack

sources.claim: The Houthis denied responsibility for the Aden airport attack

fairness.reason: Accurate as written; denial sourced.

fairness.note: Gives only the schedule and the number of candidates. Does not say that voting took place only in government-held areas, or that the Syrian opposition and the United States rejected the election as a sham or rigged (Al Jazeera; US State Department, July 2020).

sources.claim: Voting took place across government-held territory, not in opposition-held Idlib or the Kurdish-run north
The US State Department called the elections rigged
Opposition leaders called the vote a charade

fairness.reason: Omission is real; 'several Western governments' narrowed to the US, which is what was verified.

fairness.note: Almost the whole summary is criticism of the election, and some of it is in Wikipedia's own voice: the election is "highly controversial" and the disqualified candidates "popular". Leaves out the Guardian Council's position that its vetting decisions stood, and the Supreme Leader's backing of them, though he later said some candidates had been wronged (Reuters, May and June 2021).
phrases: highly controversial election
mass disqualification of popular candidates

sources.claim: Khamenei backed the Guardian Council's disqualification of candidates
